j1.what_the_patch_does: Adds an unconditional one-time retry when a request returns a bare 403 (status 403 with no headers), alongside unrelated pagination validation.
j1.reading_applied: Broad/plain reading: “Ruled out: retrying on a bare 403” prohibits retrying that response at all.
j1.rationale: The patch explicitly retries a bare 403 once. That is the exact behavior the rule ruled out; the patch’s distinction from classified 403s does not change that its added path is for a bare 403.

j2.what_the_patch_does: Adds input validation and, relevantly, retries one HTTP 403 response when its headers are empty, before classifying the response. It also adds a test for that retry.
j2.reading_applied: I applied the rule literally: a "bare 403" is a 403 without qualifying response information, and the rule rules out retrying such a response at all. The rule does not limit the prohibition to a default retry policy or repeated retries.
j2.rationale: The patch explicitly retries a 403 with no headers and labels it a "bare 403." That is the behavior the rule ruled out, because an unqualified 403 may be a permissions error for which waiting or retrying does not help.
